question.text: An SIA is comparing three legal forms — Trust, Society, and Section 8 Company. Which grouping correctly matches constituting law AND charter document?

answer.text: Trust: Companies Act 2013, Trust Deed | Society: Indian Trust Act 1882, MOA | Section 8: Societies Act 1860, AOA
Trust: Indian Trusts Act 1882, Trust Deed | Society: Societies Registration Act 1860, MOA + rules | Section 8: Companies Act 2013, MOA + AOA
Trust: Societies Act 1860, MOA | Society: Companies Act 2013, AOA | Section 8: Indian Trusts Act 1882, Trust Deed
All three are governed by the Companies Act 2013 with standardised MOA + AOA

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Table 1.1 of Ch 1: Trust → Indian Trusts Act 1882 → Trust Deed; Society → Societies Registration Act 1860 → MOA + Rules & Regulations; Section 8 Company → Companies Act 2013 → MOA + AOA. **The Trap:** Options A and C scramble the mappings. Option D incorrectly homogenises the three under one Act — in reality, each has a distinct constitutive regime. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cross-links to Ch 11 (Key Regulations). SIAs build their engagement-planning checklist around this table to drive governance and documentation review. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** During pre-engagement, request the specific charter document (Trust Deed / MOA+Rules / MOA+AOA) and verify against the latest amendments filed with the respective authority. Stale charters are a common finding — flag in the management letter.
